description: Dominated-edge filtering makes the minimal network of a simple temporal network (STN) *dispatchable* with far fewer edges. The *minimal network* has an edge with the tightest bound for every pair of time points. A network is dispatchable when an executor that only passes times to the direct neighbours of each executed point never breaks a constraint. Filtering drops each edge that a shortest path through a third point already implies: a non-negative `a → c` when a non-negative `b → c` is on such a path, and a negative `a → c` when a negative `a → b` is on it. First, each group of points with fixed offsets to each other (a *rigid component*) is tied to one leader.

papers.authors: N. Muscettola, P. Morris, I. Tsamardinos
papers.title: Reformulating temporal plans for efficient execution
Dynamic Controllability and Dispatchability Relationships
papers.venue: CPAIOR 2014, Lecture Notes in Computer Science

lineage.source: temporal-control, src/stn/dispatchable.rs: "The minimal network (all-pairs shortest paths) is dispatchable but dense. Filtering keeps a subset of its edges that is still dispatchable"; src/stn.rs computes that network with "minimal_network (Floyd-Warshall)"
